opencode.yml
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}"
on:
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Existing issue to run
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);

We have a blank canvas. Need to build a 3D WWII RTS. Let's plan the architecture carefully.

Goals:
- Playable, visually impressive 3D RTS with realistic-ish graphics (Three.js, PBR-ish lighting, shadows, terrain, fog).
- 5 factions: USA, USSR, Germany, UK, Japan.
- Skirmish mode: pick faction, enemy faction, map, difficulty, starting resources. Full RTS loop: base building, resource gathering, unit production, combat, victory.
- Campaign mode: historical missions (chronological) with briefings, objectives, scripted setups, faction per mission. e.g. 1939 Poland (Germany), 1940 Dunkirk (UK), 1941 Barbarossa (Germany), 1941 Pearl Harbor (Japan), 1942 Midway (USA), 1942 Stalingrad (USSR), 1944 Normandy (USA/UK), 1945 Berlin (USSR), 1945 Okinawa (USA). Maybe 8 missions with historical text.
- Controls: box select, right-click move/attack, camera pan (WASD/edge/drag), zoom, build menu, production queue, HUD.
- Performance: instanced/merged low-poly units, sprite-ish? Realistic graphics achievable with good lighting, terrain textures generated procedurally (canvas textures), fog, shadows, color grading. Avoid heavy assets (no downloads available maybe). Use procedural geometry for tanks, infantry, buildings. Could add nice detail: tank tracks, turrets, muzzle flashes, explosions, smoke particles, tracers, building scaffolds.

Given effort constraints, build a solid RTS with:
- Three.js from npm.
- Procedural terrain with heightmap, texture splat via vertex colors and canvas texture.
- Units as low-poly models with distinct silhouettes per faction: Sherman (US), T-34 (USSR), Panzer IV/Tiger (Germany), Churchill/Cromwell (UK), Chi-Ha (Japan), infantry squads, artillery, recon, tank destroyers maybe.
- Buildings: HQ, barracks, factory, refinery/depot, turret/AA, power? Keep economy simple: supply depots generate resources via capture points? Simpler: workers harvest from resource nodes (supply crates/oil). Classic RTS: engineers build structures, harvesters gather.

Design scope that is achievable and robust:
Core loop:
- Start with HQ, 2 harvesters (trucks), some infantry.
- Resources: "Supplies" + "Fuel"? Keep one resource "Supplies" plus "Command points" cap for units? Simpler: one resource (Supplies), pop cap from HQ + depots.
- Buildings: HQ (produces harvester, unlocks), Barracks (infantry), Factory (vehicles), Depot (resource drop + pop cap + income boost), Turret (defense). Construction: select builder (Engineer squad), click building placement, construction progresses over time, cost deducted.
- Harvesters: click resource node (supply crates scattered), auto gather, return to nearest depot/HQ.
- Units: infantry squad (riflemen), anti-tank team, tank, artillery, scout car. Faction-specific names/stats/models. Maybe 6 unit types each with faction variants. Production from barracks/factory.
- Combat: auto-acquire targets in range, turret rotation, projectiles (shells/tracers), damage types, health bars, explosions, wrecks, smoke.
- AI opponent: builds base, produces units, attacks in waves, harvests. Reasonable behavior with difficulty scaling.
- Fog of war: maybe simplified shroud (visual fog plane / grid visibility) — nice but costly. Could implement simple fog-of-war overlay with a canvas texture updated from unit positions. That's doable: 128x128 canvas texture over map, alpha black for unexplored/hidden. Renders as a plane above terrain. Actually RTS fog is great for feel. Implement with low-res grid 64x64, update per frame-ish, bilinear upscale, and hide enemy units in fog. Performance fine.
- Selection: click, drag box, control groups (1-9), double-click select same type. Right-click orders move/attack/gather/build.
- Camera: WASD/arrow, middle/right drag? Right-click is orders, so camera pan via WASD + edge scroll + middle-drag, zoom via wheel, rotate via Q/E.
- Minimap: canvas 2D rendering terrain + units, click to jump.
- UI: top resource bar, left selection panel, bottom command card, build/production buttons, tooltips, objectives panel, event log, pause menu, game over screen.
- Main menu: title with 3D background (rotating camera over battlefield), buttons: Campaign, Skirmish, Settings/Controls, Credits. Faction select cards for skirmish with flags (procedural flags via CSS/SVG), map select, difficulty.
- Campaign: mission list with historical dates/descriptions, unlock progression stored in localStorage, mission objectives, intro briefing, victory/defeat with historical epilogue. Scripted mission setups: player faction, enemy faction, map, starting forces, objectives (destroy enemy HQ, survive N minutes, capture points, escort). Keep 3 objective types.
- Audio: WebAudio procedural sounds (gunfire, explosions, engine, UI clicks, music drone). Nice to have; implement simple synthesized SFX with mute toggle.
- Realistic graphics: ACES tone mapping, soft shadows PCF, fog, hemisphere+directional light, sky gradient shader, ground with procedural noise texture, grass patches? Use instanced rocks/bushes/trees for detail. Post-processing bloom? Could add EffectComposer UnrealBloomPass + SMAA. With SwiftShader software rendering in CI it might be slow but screenshots need to work. Keep bloom optional/low res. Let's test performance. Given capture uses SwiftShader (CPU), heavy scene may render slowly. We need screenshot capture to succeed. Keep default renderer pixel ratio capped at 1.5, shadow map 2048, moderate objects. Bloom maybe skip or low. I'd rather use renderer with tone mapping and no post FX for performance, plus fog and good materials. Add vignette/color grade via CSS overlay. That gives realistic-ish look.

// ============================================================
// IRON FRONT — procedural audio (WebAudio, no external assets)
// ============================================================
export class AudioEngine {
  constructor() {
    this.ctx = null
    this.master = null
    this.noiseBuf = null
    this.ambient = null
    this.muted = localStorage.getItem('ironfront.muted') === '1'
    this.last = {}
    this.started = false
  }

  init() {
    if (this.ctx) {
      if (this.ctx.state === 'suspended') this.ctx.resume()
      return
    }
    const AC = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext
    if (!AC) return
    this.ctx = new AC()
    this.master = this.ctx.createGain()
    this.master.gain.value = this.muted ? 0 : 0.55
    this.master.connect(this.ctx.destination)
    const len = this.ctx.sampleRate * 2
    this.noiseBuf = this.ctx.createBuffer(1, len, this.ctx.sampleRate)
    const data = this.noiseBuf.getChannelData(0)
    for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1
    this.started = true
    this.startAmbient()
  }

  setMuted(m) {
    this.muted = m
    localStorage.setItem('ironfront.muted', m ? '1' : '0')
    if (this.master) this.master.gain.setTargetAtTime(m ? 0 : 0.55, this.ctx.currentTime, 0.05)
  }
  toggleMute() { this.setMuted(!this.muted); return this.muted }

  gate(key, ms) {
    if (this.muted || !this.ctx) return false
    const now = performance.now()
    if (this.last[key] && now - this.last[key] < ms) return false
    this.last[key] = now
    return true
  }

  noise(duration, gain, filterType, freq, q = 1, freqEnd = null) {
    if (!this.ctx) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime
    const src = this.ctx.createBufferSource()
    src.buffer = this.noiseBuf
    src.loop = true
    const f = this.ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    f.type = filterType
    f.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, t)
    if (freqEnd) f.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(30, freqEnd), t + duration)
    f.Q.value = q
    const g = this.ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(gain, t)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0008, t + duration)
    src.connect(f); f.connect(g); g.connect(this.master)
    src.start(t)
    src.stop(t + duration + 0.02)
  }

  tone(freq, duration, gain, type = 'sine', freqEnd = null, delay = 0) {
    if (!this.ctx) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime + delay
    const o = this.ctx.createOscillator()
    o.type = type
    o.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, t)
    if (freqEnd) o.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(20, freqEnd), t + duration)
    const g = this.ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(gain, t + 0.012)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0008, t + duration)
    o.connect(g); g.connect(this.master)
    o.start(t); o.stop(t + duration + 0.02)
  }

  play(name, opts = {}) {
    if (!this.ctx || this.muted) return
    const vol = opts.volume ?? 1
    switch (name) {
      case 'click':
        if (!this.gate('click', 40)) return
        this.tone(520, 0.05, 0.035, 'square', 380)
        break
      case 'select':
        if (!this.gate('select', 60)) return
        this.tone(340, 0.09, 0.03, 'triangle', 520)
        break
      case 'order':
        if (!this.gate('order', 90)) return
        this.tone(420, 0.06, 0.035, 'square', 620)
        this.tone(660, 0.06, 0.025, 'triangle', 520, 0.06)
        break
      case 'rifle':
        if (!this.gate('rifle', 65)) return
        this.noise(0.09, 0.10 * vol, 'highpass', 900, 0.7, 300)
        this.tone(160, 0.07, 0.03 * vol, 'square', 60)
        break
      case 'mg':
        if (!this.gate('mg', 45)) return
        this.noise(0.05, 0.07 * vol, 'bandpass', 1400, 1.4)
        break
      case 'cannon':
        if (!this.gate('cannon', 80)) return
        this.noise(0.32, 0.2 * vol, 'lowpass', 900, 0.8, 120)
        this.tone(95, 0.34, 0.16 * vol, 'sine', 38)
        break
      case 'explosion':
        if (!this.gate('explosion', 90)) return
        this.noise(0.9, 0.32 * vol, 'lowpass', 700, 0.7, 70)
        this.tone(62, 0.8, 0.22 * vol, 'sine', 24)
        break
      case 'build':
        if (!this.gate('build', 120)) return
        this.noise(0.12, 0.05 * vol, 'bandpass', 700, 2)
        this.tone(180, 0.1, 0.03, 'square', 150)
        break
      case 'complete':
        this.tone(523, 0.16, 0.05, 'triangle')
        this.tone(784, 0.24, 0.045, 'triangle', null, 0.12)
        break
      case 'ready':
        this.tone(660, 0.09, 0.035, 'triangle')
        break
      case 'error':
        if (!this.gate('error', 200)) return
        this.tone(120, 0.16, 0.05, 'square', 90)
        break
      case 'alarm':
        if (!this.gate('alarm', 1600)) return
        this.tone(440, 0.35, 0.05, 'sawtooth', 620)
        this.tone(440, 0.35, 0.05, 'sawtooth', 620, 0.42)
        break
      case 'victory':
        this.tone(392, 0.5, 0.08, 'triangle')
        this.tone(523, 0.5, 0.08, 'triangle', null, 0.16)
        this.tone(659, 0.7, 0.08, 'triangle', null, 0.32)
        this.tone(784, 1.2, 0.07, 'sine', null, 0.48)
        break
      case 'defeat':
        this.tone(196, 0.7, 0.09, 'sine', 146)
        this.tone(146, 0.9, 0.08, 'sine', 110, 0.5)
        this.tone(98, 1.4, 0.07, 'sine', 73, 1.0)
        break
      case 'engine':
        if (!this.gate('engine', 400)) return
        this.tone(55, 0.5, 0.03, 'sawtooth', 70)
        break
      default:
        break
    }
  }

  startAmbient() {
    if (!this.ctx || this.ambient) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime
    const src = this.ctx.createBufferSource()
    src.buffer = this.noiseBuf
    src.loop = true
    const f = this.ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    f.type = 'lowpass'
    f.frequency.value = 320
    const g = this.ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.value = 0.028
    src.connect(f); f.connect(g); g.connect(this.master)
    src.start(t)
    const drone = this.ctx.createOscillator()
    drone.type = 'sine'
    drone.frequency.value = 48
    const dg = this.ctx.createGain()
    dg.gain.value = 0.012
    const lfo = this.ctx.createOscillator()
    lfo.frequency.value = 0.07
    const lg = this.ctx.createGain()
    lg.gain.value = 0.007
    lfo.connect(lg); lg.connect(dg.gain)
    drone.connect(dg); dg.connect(this.master)
    drone.start(t); lfo.start(t)
    this.ambient = { src, drone, lfo, g, dg }
  }

  stopAmbient() {
    if (!this.ambient) return
    try {
      this.ambient.src.stop()
      this.ambient.drone.stop()
      this.ambient.lfo.stop()
    } catch (e) { /* already stopped */ }
    this.ambient = null
  }
}

Entity base:
```js
let ENTITY_ID = 1;

   this.game=game; this.id=...; this.faction=faction; this.team=team; this.def=def;

```
Team = 'player'|'enemy'. Colors ring: player blue, enemy red. But player is always team player. Faction paint on model.

Selection ring: `RingGeometry(radius*0.95, radius*1.12, 28)` rotated flat, material MeshBasicMaterial color, transparent .75, depthWrite false, polygonOffset. Add to scene (not group?) If added to group, it moves with unit and sits at y=0.1 relative; group y = terrain height. Good. But units tilt? no. Add to group at y=0.08. Enemy rings maybe not shown unless selected. Hide rings for unselected. For selected multiple, show. Health bars show when damaged/selected.

Health bar: group with two planes, each material MeshBasicMaterial depthTest false. Background plane 1.5x0.16, fill 1.5x0.12 offset x? To scale fill from left, geometry translated +0.75? Create PlaneGeometry(1,0.12) translated +0.5 in x then scale.x; position x=-0.75. Simpler use Sprite? Sprites always face camera and scale, but fill anchored center. Use Mesh planes with billboard quaternion; set fill mesh scale.x = ratio, position.x = -width/2 + width*ratio/2. Update each frame. Use shared geometries but separate materials for colors. Colors: green/yellow/red based hp; set material color per entity (material per entity). Fine.

Group position: entity.group at ground height. Mesh hull at local y=0. For infantry, mesh at y=0. Health bar at y=height+0.6. Selection ring at y=0.08.

Unit class:
```js
class Unit extends Entity {
  constructor(game, faction, team, type, x, z) {
    const stats = unitStats(faction,type);
    super(...stats)
    this.type=type; this.stats=stats; this.speed=stats.speed; this.range=stats.range; ...

Movement:
```
update(dt) {
 if (!alive) return;
 this.attackCooldown -= dt;
 this.acquireTimer -= dt;
 ...
 this.think(dt)
 this.updateMovement(dt)
 this.updateCombat(dt)
 this.updateVisual(dt)
}
```
Movement target `this.moveTarget` {x,z}. Order types:
- 'move': move to point; on arrive -> idle.
- 'attackMove': move to point, engage enemies encountered; resume after kill.
- 'attack': chase target until in range, then stop and fire.
- 'gather': harvester FSM.
- 'build': engineer moves to building site, then builds.
- 'hold': no movement, auto-attack in range.
- 'idle': auto-acquire, small chase.
- 'return' etc for harvester.

Simplify with `order = {type, x, z, target, building}`.

State machine:
```
update(dt) {
  if harvester -> updateHarvester
  else {
    handle order
    acquire targets
    fire
  }
  movement
}
```

Common targeting:
- `findTarget(range, preferArmor)` using game.enemyUnits/buildings for team. Search units and buildings within range; choose nearest; prefer vehicle if AT.

{type:'move', x,z}
{type:'attackMove', x,z}
{type:'attack', target}
{type:'hold'}
{type:'gather', node}
{type:'build', building}
{type:'idle'}
```
`this.target` is combat target (entity). 

Each update:
1. if order.type === 'attack': if target invalid -> idle; else if distance > range*0.92 -> move toward target; else stop and fire. 
2. attackMove: if target valid and within vision -> stop and fire; if no target, move to point; on arrive idle. Auto acquire each 0.35s within vision. If target found, set state; after target dead, resume move.
3. move: no auto attack? RTS usually units don't stop to attack on move but can fire while moving if in range? Keep auto-fire at targets in range while moving (turrets can), but don't chase. 
4. idle/hold: acquire within vision; if target in range fire; if target beyond range but within vision and order not hold, chase up to 14 from home? Let's implement idle units chase up to 12 units from their current position (leash) then return. Simpler: idle units do not chase, only fire in range. This is predictable. Attack-move for offense.
5. gather/build handled.

Firing:
- if target in range and (for turret units) aim tolerance? Ignore aim tolerance, just fire when cooldown ready; rotate turret visually toward target.
- muzzle position: from turret barrel tip in world. Compute using group matrix: local offset (0, turretY+0.6, barrel length + 1) rotated by group + turret. Use `new Vector3(...).applyAxisAngle(Y, heading+turretAngle).add(pos)`. Height = group y + turretY + 0.6.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D WWII RTS with realistic presentation, five factions, skirmish mode, and historically themed campaign content.

## Requirements
- Factions: America, Soviet Union, Germany, England, and Japan.
- Include skirmish mode.
- Include a campaign based on historical WWII operations.
- Build and make it playable now.

## Decisions
- Use a React-free Vite/Three.js implementation with procedural models and Web Audio.
- Use a military-archive visual style with faction-specific UI and procedural battlefield presentation.
- Use in-repository gameplay systems rather than external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite project scaffold and base HTML, CSS, and package configuration.
- WWII menu and faction/setup UI structure.
- Core data model for factions, units, buildings, maps, and historical operations.
- Procedural Three.js model library for units and structures.
- Battlefield world builder with terrain, sky, lighting, props, and minimap support.
- Procedural battle effects and Web Audio engine.
- Entity system with units, buildings, supply, harvesting, combat, production, and destruction.
- Enemy AI commander with economy, construction, production, defense, attack, and regroup behavior.

### Active
- Integration of the game systems into the main application loop and playable screen.

### Blocked
- The game was interrupted before completing and verifying the main application integration and runtime.

## Next Move
1. Complete `src/main.js` integration of menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, and HUD.
2. Install dependencies and run `npm run build` to identify module or syntax errors.
3. Start the app and perform browser-based gameplay checks.
4. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot; correct visible layout or rendering failures.
5. Verify faction selection, skirmish start, unit construction, selection, movement, combat, and victory/defeat behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: project scripts and dependencies.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game UI screen structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: complete visual and responsive UI styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js`: factions, maps, operations, units, and buildings.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`: procedural Three.js faction models.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: terrain, environment, battlefield, and minimap construction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: explosions, smoke, tracers, wrecks, decals, and impacts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities.js`: gameplay units and structures.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ai.js`: enemy economy and military commander.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural Web Audio system.

## Important Context
- The implementation is in progress and has not yet been fully integrated or launched.
- `src/world.js` now uses `mergeGeometries` directly.
- Unit destruction logic and vehicle wreck creation were added to `src/entities.js`.
- The AI controller supports selectable enemy factions and difficulty-driven aggression.
- Build and runtime verification remain required.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D WWII RTS with realistic presentation, five factions, skirmish mode, and historically themed campaign content.

## Requirements
- Include playable factions for America, Soviet Union, Germany, England, and Japan.
- Include skirmish mode and historical campaign operations.
- Build the game for use now and verify its gameplay and runtime.

## Decisions
- Use a React-free Vite/Three.js implementation with procedural models and Web Audio.
- Use a military-archive visual style with faction-specific UI and procedural battlefield presentation.
- Keep gameplay systems in-repository rather than using external assets.
- Use the existing faction, unit, building, map, mission, AI, effects, world, and audio modules.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite project scaffold and package configuration.
- WWII menu, faction setup, skirmish setup, campaign, briefing, HUD, and manual UI structure.
- Faction, unit, building, map, supply, difficulty, and historical mission data.
- Procedural Three.js faction models and battlefield world builder.
- Battle effects, particle/Wreck systems, Web Audio, entity gameplay, harvesting, construction, combat, and enemy AI.
- `src/world.js` updated to use `mergeGeometries` directly.
- Unit destruction and vehicle wreck creation added to `src/entities.js`.
- Enemy AI supports faction selection and difficulty-driven production and aggression.

### Active
- Identify and integrate `src/main.js`, which is currently absent.
- Wire menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, HUD, and the application loop together.

### Blocked
- No main application module exists yet, so the game integration and runtime remain unverified.
- Build, browser gameplay verification, screenshot review, and victory/defeat verification are pending.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` and integrate all existing gameplay and UI systems.
2. Install dependencies and run `npm run build`.
3. Start the app and perform browser-based gameplay checks.
4. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot; correct visible layout or rendering failures.
5. Verify faction selection, skirmish start, unit construction, selection, movement, combat, and victory/defeat behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: Missing integration entry point to create.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Screen structure, HUD, modals, and module entry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Complete game and menu presentation styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities.js`: Units, buildings, projectiles, supply nodes, and destruction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: Terrain, environment, battlefield, scenery, and minimap support.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js`: Factions, units, structures, maps, difficulties, and campaign missions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`: Procedural faction models and shared materials.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ai.js`: Enemy economy, construction, production, attack, and regroup logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: Explosions, smoke, tracers, wrecks, decals, and impacts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: Procedural Web Audio engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite scripts and dependencies.

## Important Context
- The implementation is unfinished specifically because `src/main.js` has not been created.
- The required verification workflow is: build, run, browser check, small JPEG inspection, then gameplay verification.

## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable 3D WWII RTS with five factions, skirmish mode, and historically themed campaign content.

## Requirements
- Include America, Soviet Union, Germany, England, and Japan as playable factions.
- Include skirmish mode and historical campaign operations.
- Build the game and verify gameplay and runtime.

## Decisions
- Use a React-free Vite/Three.js implementation with procedural models and Web Audio.
- Keep gameplay systems and assets in the repository.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite scaffold, UI screens, game data, procedural world/models, gameplay entities, effects, audio, and enemy AI are present.
- `src/world.js` uses `mergeGeometries`; `src/entities.js` creates vehicle wrecks on destruction; AI supports faction and difficulty selection.

### Active
- Integrate the existing systems in `src/main.js`, which is currently absent.

### Blocked
- Runtime integration and verification are blocked until `src/main.js` is created.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` to connect menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, HUD, and the application loop.
2. Run `npm run build` and resolve any errors.
3. Launch the app and check the browser experience; save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.
4. Verify faction selection, skirmish start, construction, selection, movement, combat, and victory/defeat.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Missing application entry point and integration.
- `index.html`: Screen structure, HUD, modals, and module entry.
- `src/style.css`: Menu and game presentation.
- `src/entities.js`: Units, buildings, projectiles, and supply nodes.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain, scenery, battlefield, and minimap.

## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable 3D WWII RTS with five factions, skirmish mode, and historically themed campaign content.

## Requirements
- Include America, Soviet Union, Germany, England, and Japan as playable factions.
- Include skirmish mode and historical campaign operations.
- Build the game and verify gameplay and runtime.

## Decisions
- Use a React-free Vite/Three.js implementation with procedural models and Web Audio.
- Keep gameplay systems and assets in the repository.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the Vite scaffold and UI screens.
- Implemented faction, unit, structure, map, and campaign data.
- Added procedural terrain, scenery, battlefield models, and minimap support.
- Implemented units, buildings, projectiles, supply nodes, wrecks, explosions, smoke, tracers, impacts, and audio.
- Implemented faction-aware enemy AI with difficulty selection.
- Confirmed `src/world.js` uses `mergeGeometries`.

### Active
- Integrate the complete application in `src/main.js`.

### Blocked
- Runtime integration and verification remain blocked until `src/main.js` exists and is wired into the app.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` to connect menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, HUD, and the application loop.
2. Run `npm run build` and resolve build errors.
3. Launch the app, verify the browser experience, and save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.
4. Verify faction selection, skirmish start, construction, selection, movement, combat, and victory/defeat.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Missing application entry point and integration.
- `index.html`: Screen structure, HUD, modals, and module entry.
- `src/style.css`: Menu and game presentation.
- `src/entities.js`: Units, buildings, projectiles, and supply nodes.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain, scenery, battlefield, and minimap.
- `src/data.js`: Factions, units, structures, maps, and campaign missions.
- `src/ai.js`: Enemy economy, production, attacks, and regrouping.
- `src/effects.js`: Explosions, smoke, tracers, wrecks, and impacts.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural Web Audio engine.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- `src/world.js` exports `createWorld(scene, mapDef, options)`.
- `src/entities.js` exports `Unit`, `Building`, `Projectile`, and `SupplyNode`.
- `src/effects.js` exports `Effects` and must be updated alongside entity destruction effects.
- `src/ai.js` reads `game.enemyFaction`, `game.difficulty`, `game.enemyBase`, and team economy/army state.
- The application entry point currently does not exist.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable 3D WWII RTS with five factions, skirmish mode, and historically themed campaign content.

## Requirements
- Include America, Soviet Union, Germany, England, and Japan as playable factions.
- Include skirmish mode and historical campaign operations.
- Build the game and verify gameplay and runtime.

## Decisions
- Use a React-free Vite/Three.js implementation with procedural models and Web Audio.
- Keep gameplay systems and assets in the repository.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the Vite scaffold and UI screens.
- Implemented faction, unit, structure, map, and campaign data.
- Added procedural terrain, scenery, battlefield models, and minimap support.
- Implemented units, buildings, projectiles, supply nodes, wrecks, explosions, smoke, tracers, impacts, and audio.
- Implemented faction-aware enemy AI with difficulty selection.
- Confirmed `src/world.js` uses `mergeGeometries`.
- Set up `index.html` to load `src/main.js`, though the entry point still needs implementation.

### Active
- Integrate the complete application in `src/main.js`.
- Wire menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, HUD, and the application loop.

### Blocked
- Runtime integration and browser verification remain blocked until `src/main.js` exists and is wired into the app.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` to connect the menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, HUD, and application loop.
2. Run `npm run build` and resolve build errors.
3. Launch the app, verify the browser experience, and save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.
4. Verify faction selection, skirmish start, construction, selection, movement, combat, and victory/defeat.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Missing application entry point and integration target.
- `index.html`: Screen structure, HUD, modals, and module entry.
- `src/entities.js`: Units, buildings, projectiles, and supply nodes.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain, scenery, battlefield, and minimap.
- `src/data.js`: Factions, units, structures, maps, and campaign missions.
- `src/ai.js`: Enemy economy, production, attacks, and regrouping.
- `src/effects.js`: Explosions, smoke, tracers, wrecks, and impacts.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural Web Audio engine.
- `src/style.css`: Menu and game presentation.

## Important Context
- `src/world.js` exports `createWorld(scene, mapDef, options)`.
- `src/entities.js` exports `Unit`, `Building`, `Projectile`, and `SupplyNode`.
- `src/effects.js` must remain synchronized with entity destruction effects.
- `src/ai.js` reads `game.enemyFaction`, `game.difficulty`, `game.enemyBase`, and team economy/army state.
- `package.json` provides `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, and `npm run preview`; Vite serves on port 3002.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable 3D WWII RTS with five factions, skirmish mode, and historical campaign operations.

## Requirements
- Include America, Soviet Union, Germany, England, and Japan as playable factions.
- Include skirmish mode and historical campaign operations.
- Build the game and verify gameplay and runtime.

## Decisions
- Use a React-free Vite/Three.js implementation with procedural models and Web Audio.
- Keep gameplay systems and assets in the repository.
- Integrate all existing systems through `src/main.js` as the application entry point.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the Vite scaffold and UI screens.
- Implemented faction, unit, structure, map, and campaign data.
- Added procedural terrain, scenery, battlefield models, fog of war, and minimap support.
- Implemented units, buildings, projectiles, supply nodes, wrecks, explosions, smoke, tracers, impacts, and audio.
- Implemented faction-aware enemy AI with difficulty selection.
- Created `src/main.js` and wired menu, skirmish setup, campaign, world, entities, AI, HUD, and the application loop.

### Active
- Validate `src/main.js` integration and resolve build/runtime issues.

### Blocked
- Browser verification, gameplay verification, and screenshot inspection remain blocked until the build is resolved and the app can run.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and resolve integration errors.
2. Launch the app and verify the browser experience and a small JPEG screenshot.
3. Verify faction selection, skirmish start, construction, selection, movement, combat, and victory/defeat.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Missing entry point has now been created and is the primary integration target.
- `index.html`: Screen structure, HUD, modals, and module entry.
- `src/entities.js`: Units, buildings, projectiles, and supply nodes.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain, scenery, battlefield, and minimap.
- `src/data.js`: Factions, units, structures, maps, difficulty levels, and campaigns.
- `src/ai.js`: Enemy economy, production, attacks, and regrouping.
- `src/effects.js`: Explosion, smoke, wreck, tracer, and impact effects.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural Web Audio engine.

## Important Context
- `src/world.js` exports `createWorld(scene, mapDef, options)`.
- `src/entities.js` exports `Unit`, `Building`, `Projectile`, and `SupplyNode`.
- `src/effects.js` must remain synchronized with entity destruction effects.
- `src/ai.js` reads `game.enemyFaction`, `game.difficulty`, `game.enemyBase`, and team economy/army state.
- Package scripts serve Vite on port 3002 via `npm run dev`/`npm run preview`.
